outside_band_and_explained.CodeLoad: 0.9866 against a per-benchmark A/A band of +-0.49%. Real, and the mechanism is known and documented (11.5 F0b accounting): the F0b decode layer costs compile-path work. This is the clause 11 item that does not pass on its own terms.

outside_band_without_a_mechanism.DeltaBlue: 0.9879 in the suite run; a dedicated n=20 run with an in-run A/A control (A/A -0.07%) put it at -0.54%, and splitting the campaign at ef7fc62a attributes -0.34% to the FIRST half (id reclaim, with_* merge, R0, F0a) and -0.03% to F0b.
outside_band_without_a_mechanism.RegExp: 0.9873 in the suite run, but NOT reliably measurable at this effect size: two independent dedicated runs gave -0.89% and -1.66%, and the split reading was +1.88% then -3.47%. Recorded as unresolved rather than as a number.
outside_band_without_a_mechanism.interpretation: The same A/B moved EarleyBoyer +1.09%, SplayLatency +1.46%, Typescript +0.77% and PdfJS +0.65% in the other direction, with no mechanism either. Mixed signs, no mechanism, cancelling to zero at the composite is the handler-island layout signature that 11.5 clause 10 exists to keep out of carrier judgements: the first half of the campaign deletes or merges handlers (nip1 retired, set_proto demoted, five ids reclaimed, with_* 5->1, R0), and every deletion shifts the address of every other handler.

verdict: informational for the line as a whole (parity); the CodeLoad row is the evidence behind the 11.5 clause 11 item recorded as NOT passed for F0b
